title: Glaze a window: set two setting blocks, then stand the glass unit on them
instruction: Put the two black setting blocks on the white marks in the frame, then lower the glass unit straight down into the frame so it stands on both blocks and never touches the sill.
context: Glaziers (O*NET 47-2121) stand an insulated glass unit on two setting blocks placed at its quarter points, so that its weight never bears on the frame's sill or on one corner: glass whose bottom edge comes down on the metal sill, or that rests on a single point, can chip, crack or lose its seal. The blocks go in first, then the unit is lowered straight down into the glazing channel until it stands on them. Here one arm sets the blocks and the other carries and lowers the glass. The whole trial is watched, not only its end: glass set in first and propped up on blocks pushed in afterwards has already touched the sill.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Five kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Frame: the bottom of a window frame in grey (sRGB 0.60, 0.62, 0.65) aluminium, fixed to the table, centred at x 30.0 cm, y 0: a sill 60 mm along x, 260 mm along y and 10 mm tall; standing on the sill, two glazing stops (walls 8 mm thick along x, 260 mm long along y, 40 mm tall) whose inner faces are at x 28.0 and 32.0 cm, leaving a 40 mm wide channel along y with its floor (the sill's top) 10 mm above the table and the stops' tops 50 mm above it; and two jambs (40 mm along x, 10 mm along y, 60 mm tall) standing on the sill between the stops with their inner faces at y -12.0 and +12.0 cm, closing the channel's ends, so the channel is 240 mm long and open at the top. (2) Two quarter-point marks: thin white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.95) plastic plates, 24 mm along x, 30 mm along y and 1 mm thick, fixed on the sill in the channel, centred at x 30.0 cm, y -5.0 and +5.0 cm (the quarter points of a 200 mm unit centred in the channel). (3) Block tray: a dark grey (sRGB 0.30, 0.30, 0.32) plastic plate 90 x 90 x 4 mm, fixed, centred at x 20.0 cm, y -24.0 cm. (4) Two setting blocks: loose black (sRGB 0.08, 0.08, 0.08) neoprene rubber blocks, 24 mm along x, 30 mm along y and 8 mm tall, 7 g each, lying flat on the tray side by side, centred at x 18.0 and 22.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y. (5) Glass unit: a loose small double-glazed unit (two 2 mm panes on a 20 mm aluminium spacer), 24 mm thick, 200 mm long and 80 mm tall, 0.20 kg, pale blue-grey (sRGB 0.75, 0.85, 0.90), standing on one of its 24 x 200 mm long edges on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm (its ends at y +19.0 and +39.0 cm), its length along y and its faces normal to x; for real trials, a stand-in of the same size and mass (acrylic panes on a weighted spacer) is safer than glass. With a top-down grasp only the right arm reaches the blocks and only the left arm reaches the glass unit: near the table the left arm reaches no further right than about y -18 cm at x 18 cm, short of the blocks' nearer sides at y -22.5 cm, and the right arm no further left than about y +17 cm at x 21 cm, short of the unit's nearer end at y +19 cm. An arm stretched across with its gripper turned sideways could reach further. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial, once per control step (20 Hz). 'The channel' is the space between the stops' inner faces (x 28.0 to 32.0 cm) and the jambs' inner faces (y -12.0 to +12.0 cm). 'Touched the sill' means that at some step a corner of the glass unit inside the channel's outline (2 mm slack) was less than 2 mm above the sill's top (1 mm above the marks' top); a unit standing on a block is at least 8 mm up. The unit's 'tilt' is the angle of its 80 mm height axis from vertical (either long edge down; lying on a face or stood on a 24 x 80 mm end is 90 degrees). 'In the channel' means all eight corners of the unit lie inside the channel's outline seen from above (1 mm slack); 'standing in the channel' means in the channel with a tilt under 3 degrees. A block 'lies on the sill' when its 8 mm axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either broad face down), its lowest point is between 1 mm below and 3 mm above the sill's top and its centre is inside the channel. A block is 'set' on a mark when it lies on the sill, its sides are within 15 degrees of the channel's and its centre is within 8 mm of the mark's centre horizontally; 'both blocks set' means one on each mark. The unit 'rests on' a block when that block lies on the sill, at least half of the block's top seen from above is under the unit's underside, and the unit's underside is within 2 mm of the block's top there (above or below). 'Off centre' is the distance along y of the unit's centre from the channel's centre (8 mm off leaves 12 mm to each jamb). Score 0 if the unit touched the sill at any moment, whatever happens afterwards, or if at the end it is tilted more than 30 degrees or is off the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top). Otherwise: 1.0 if both blocks are set and the unit stands in the channel resting on both blocks, at most 8 mm off centre; 0.75 if the unit stands in the channel resting on both blocks, the blocks are within 20 mm of their marks' centres (one on each mark, sides within 15 degrees) and it is at most 15 mm off centre, but the 1.0 limits are not met; 0.5 if the unit stands in the channel resting on at least one block but does not meet 0.75; 0.25 if both blocks are set but the unit does not stand in the channel on a block (not brought over, held above the blocks, or leaning in the channel); 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early (success) once the 1.0 conditions have held with the unit and both blocks still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 3 s, longer than the scripted demo takes to settle and open its fingers once the glass is down (2 s), so it cannot end while the gripper still holds the unit; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. In a real trial, chalk the unit's bottom edge: a print on the sill outside the blocks shows a touch; the blocks' offsets and the unit's centring are read with a ruler against the marks and the jambs.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with default friction. The frame, marks and tray are fixed; the blocks are rigid (real neoprene gives slightly under load) and the glass unit is one opaque uniform-density box of the stated size and mass, without separate panes, spacer or seal. No glazing beads, tape or sealant: the stops only keep the unit upright. Breakage is not simulated. The scorer cannot see the grippers: glass held still within 2 mm of the blocks counts as resting on them.
reset_notes: Put the two setting blocks back flat on the tray, centred at x 18.0 and 22.0 cm, y -24.0 cm, their 30 mm sides along y, and the glass unit back standing on a long edge on the table, centred at x 22.0 cm, y +29.0 cm, its faces normal to x. Nothing is consumed (in a real build, wipe any chalk off the sill).
